item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-25
item.description: One sentence from a WeChat post settles this morning, and it is six hundred characters long. On 2026-11-20, at the third Open Source Technology Academic Forum inside the OpenAtom Developer Conference in Zhengzhou, the China Electronics Standardization Institute (电子标准院) and the OpenAtom Foundation jointly announced the establishment of an Open Source Standards Working Group (开源标准工作组). Its stated task: build a mechanism for converting de facto open-source standards (开源事实标准转化工作机制) and form a closed loop described in eight characters — standards carry open source, open source verifies standards (标准带开源、开源验标准) — converting a batch of good, active open-source projects into standards that industry agrees on, and then moving mature practice upward through group, industry, national and international standards in order. The announcement exists in exactly one place: the Institute's own WeChat account, published the day the feed was collected, and no second institutional source in this run has it. Read carefully, it is not a grant of authority to a community; it is a statement that the community's output will be treated as the raw material for a standards pipeline, and that the pipeline's direction is upward. The same morning, five more projects entered the same foundation's incubation and Zhengzhou signed a city-level open-source co-construction project. The foundation's count is now 64 and the ratio that would tell anyone whether that matters has never been published.
